Seller retitled this listing; chart name no longer appears in the title
history.details: Observed, stated as fact and not as a finding about the seller's reasons. The listing is STILL LIVE -- its URL answers HTTP 200 -- but the title has changed from "Inkandeszenz\u2122", as recorded on this case when it was found on 2026-11-19, to "Incandescence\u2122". The seller's own feed gives the change time as 2026-11-25T08:06:30-05:00, this morning. The URL handle is unchanged and still reads "inkandeszenz\u2122", so the original name survives in the address. "Inkandeszenz" is on the Master Trademark Filing Chart as Pending, owner/breeder Rosen Tantau KG; "Incandescence" is NOT on the chart -- checked against all 273 chart names today. The two are commonly used as the German and English trade names of the same variety, but that is horticultural background, not something Rose Watch has verified about this plant. CONSEQUENCE FOR FUTURE RUNS: this listing will report as absent from the seller's matched products every run from now on while remaining live, exactly as SPRINGLAND-008 has since 2026-11-16. It is not removed and must not be recorded as removed. Nothing about the case was altered: the originally recorded title, price, evidence, review status and case number are unchanged, and the screenshot captured on 2026-11-19 remains the record of what this listing said while it carried the chart name. Two further observations from the same check, both verified directly: the PRICE IS UNCHANGED at USD 59.99 and the product form is unchanged ("3 GALLON POTTED ROSE - Ships Spring 2027"), so nothing about what is being sold appears to have changed -- only what it is called. The DESCRIPTION was rewritten too, not just the title: the text recorded on this case opens "Inkandeszenz radiates quiet brilliance, its luminous white petals unfurling..." and the live page now opens "Incandescence\u2122 radiates quiet brilliance, its luminous white petals unfurling..." -- the same sentence with the name substituted, and replaced at each later mention as well. A second screenshot was captured today under the standing rule that a case is re-shot on a material change, so this case now carries evidence of both states: 2026-11-19 while titled "Inkandeszenz\u2122" and 2026-11-25 as "Incandescence\u2122".

history.details: Observed, and stated as fact only. This case was opened on 2026-11-19 on the title "Inkandeszenz\u2122". The seller retitled it to "Incandescence\u2122" on 2026-11-25. The chart Damon supplied that same day, ingested 2026-11-25 and in force from today's run, ADDS "Incandescence" as a Pending mark (App. Ser. No. 50233224, filed 2026-11-23, Rosen Tantau KG) and separately moves "Inkandeszenz" to Registered (Reg. No. 8550260, registered 2026-11-17). So today's crawl matched this same listing again -- same URL, whose handle still reads "inkandeszenz\u2122" -- this time on the chart name "Incandescence". It was correctly NOT treated as a new finding: the URL already carries this case, so no second case was created and the case number is unchanged. BOTH of this listing's titles are now chart names, with different statuses: the title it carried when the case was opened is Registered, and the title it carries now is Pending. This case keeps matched_trademark "Inkandeszenz" and the Registered status it took from that record; the match on "Incandescence" is recorded here rather than by changing the case's matched name, because a case's recorded match is what it was opened on. For the avoidance of doubt about the sequence, which is dates only and carries no inference about what the seller knew or intended: Inkandeszenz registered 2026-11-17; this case opened 2026-11-19; Francis Roses filed for Incandescence 2026-11-23; the seller retitled 2026-11-25 at 08:06:30-05:00 by its own feed timestamp; the chart carrying both arrived 2026-11-25. What that means is for Francis Roses or counsel to judge and is not judged here.
